description:
In this episode, Andrea Griffiths sits down with Patrick Nikoletich to unpack the Microsoft Copilot harness. Discover how teams are using the harness for non-coding scenarios, autonomous software factories, and customizing the harness for custom agents. Patrick demos a Dockerized agent worker pool, explains credential-safe inference gateways, and shows how the Agent Host Protocol (AHP) tunnels CLI sessions into isolated containers. Explore what is coming in Copilot harness 2.0, from a Rust rewrite to direct Azure tunneling.

Microsoft Copilot harness: https://gh.io/harness
Microsoft Copilot SDK: https://aka.ms/copilot-harness/sdk/repo

title: Inside the Microsoft Copilot Harness: Customizing AI Agents

It’s 2 a.m. You’re deep in a solo coding session, and your IDE doesn’t notice you haven’t moved in an hour, but the golden retriever on your desk does. In this GitHub Universe 2026 session, Yunika Liu introduces Coco, a pixel-art golden retriever that lives on a desktop window and an LED display to encourage you while you build. Discover how she used GitHub Copilot and Model Context Protocol (MCP) support to build a custom server featuring WebSocket sync, animation triggers, and music composition in just one week. Learn how anyone can connect AI coding agents to custom hardware and build their own MCP server.  

Speakers: 
Yunika Liu, Product Builder, Independent

How did a simple conference lanyard tag evolve into a full-fledged portable computer running Doom? On the GitHub Podcast, Martin Woodward breaks down the engineering journey behind the GitHub Universe badge, from early e-ink prototypes built with Pimoroni to full color screens powered by the RP2040 chip. Discover how the hardware team solved real battery safety challenges and why they added an accelerometer to automatically flip the screen 180 degrees whenever you look down at it.
